A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, Learning to Steer Learners in Games, and their complete main texts and appendices are readable. The original auxiliary proofs in v1 Appendix F are retained in v2 Appendix G; v2 inserts numerical experiments as Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 contains theoretical guarantees, constructed proof examples and algorithm pseudocode, but no original experimental or simulation outcomes, including in its appendices.

after.justification: v2 Appendix F reports original simulations of binary-search steering and payoff-recovery steering, with payoff and strategy trajectories in Figures 3–6.

M1.justification: The steering algorithms retain their structure, but Section 6.2 changes the specified learner objective from a negative to a positive regularization term: v1 Equation (25) becomes v2 Equation (26). The gradient-recovery derivation changes accordingly, although Algorithm 5 retains the old negative sign.

E1.justification: v1 has no empirical evaluation coverage. v2 Appendix F evaluates matching pennies and three constructed 2-by-2 games, covering zero-sum and general-sum interactions with OGD and stochastic mirror-descent learners. These introduce actual simulated test scenarios beyond the retained theoretical examples.

E2.justification: v2 adds one evaluated baseline, Online Gradient Descent (OGD), against binary-search steering in the three games of Appendix F.1 and Figures 3–5. v1 contains no empirical baseline comparisons; the payoff-recovery experiment compares pessimism settings rather than additional methods.

E3.justification: v2 introduces finite-horizon evaluation protocols tracking both players' payoffs and strategy coordinates, plus average optimizer payoff in Figure 4. Settings include OGD step sizes eta_0/sqrt(t), binary-search margin d=0.01, and KL-regularized mirror descent with k=50 exploration steps per optimizer action. v1 has no corresponding experimental protocols.

E4.justification: Appendix F.2 adds a targeted sensitivity analysis using pessimism margins d=0.01, 0.02 and 0.05. Figure 6 tests how the margin affects learner response speed and eventual optimizer payoff. No corresponding empirical sensitivity analysis appears in v1.

E5.justification: Neither version reports empirical run counts, seeds, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests. v2's new trajectory plots add no uncertainty-reporting practice; the theoretical high-probability guarantees already appear in v1.

E6.justification: Figures 3–6 add entirely new outcomes: reduced oscillation under binary-search steering, higher eventual optimizer payoffs in the constructed comparisons, and faster learner response with greater pessimism. These are new simulations, not improvements over v1 measurements. One added numerical statement is inconsistent: F.1 reports instance 2's Stackelberg value as 2, whereas Equations (138), (140) and Figure 5 imply 7/3.

T1.justification: The central theorems, assumptions and asymptotic rates are retained. v2 corrects a missing T factor in Appendix B.2, replaces the learner payoff matrix B with optimizer matrix A and infinite sums with finite-horizon sums in E.1, and revises the mirror-ascent KKT signs in E.2. Additional explicit-constant theorem statements largely elaborate existing arguments.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list and conclusion retain the same claims: impossibility against general no-regret learners, sufficient recovery conditions, and steering guarantees for ascending and mirror-ascent learners. The simulations support these existing contributions without redefining their scope.

C2.justification: Appendix F.1 explains that steering can outperform OGD even when OGD converges, because its Nash outcome can have lower optimizer utility. F.2 adds a mechanism explanation for the convergence-speed versus eventual-payoff tradeoff in pessimism. Section 5.1 also qualifies learner indifference at equilibrium from 'must' to 'usually'.

D1.justification: The new experiments disclose payoff matrices, the OGD step-size schedule, binary-search accuracy, the KL regularizer and exploration budget. Reproducibility information remains limited: numerical eta_0 values, initialization, and the stochastic mirror-descent noise and step-size settings are not supplied. Neither PDF provides code-access instructions.

R1.justification: v2 adds discussion or citations to Lin and Chen (2024), Foerster et al. (2017), Lu et al. (2022), Bajaj et al. (2024), and Lattimore and Szepesvari (2019). These connect the work to principal-agent learning, opponent shaping, related impossibility constructions and facet definitions; the central research positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order are preserved. v2 adds a proof sketch, illustrative examples, parameter-choice explanations, proof cross-references and acknowledgements. It inserts an experimental appendix and relabels the retained auxiliary-proof appendix from F to G, without broadly rewriting the narrative.

P2.justification: v2 adds six figures where v1 has no plots: two geometric illustrations of facets and pessimism, and four simulation figures with payoff/strategy panels, legends, exploration shading and equilibrium reference lines. This substantially expands the paper's visual explanation and evidence presentation.

improvement.justification: v2 improves accessibility and assessability through geometric illustrations, clearer derivation details and simulations demonstrating finite-horizon behavior and the pessimism tradeoff. The gain is limited by incomplete experimental settings and unresolved inconsistencies: the corrected mirror-ascent derivation conflicts with Algorithm 5's retained negative sign, and F.1 misstates one Stackelberg payoff. The revision provides useful clarification and illustration without establishing substantially stronger overall validation.
